questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A standard round bottom triangular canal section as shown in the figure has a bed slope of 1 in 200. Consider the Chezy’s coefficient as 150 m¹/²/s.




The normal depth of flow, \( y \) (in meters) for carrying a discharge of 20 m³/s is ____________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Open Channel Flow | Uniform Flow

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Standard round bottom triangular canal section
    • Bed slope \(S = 1/200\)
    • Chezy's coefficient \(C = 150\) m\(^{1/2}\)/s
    • Discharge \(Q = 20\) m³/s
  • Aim: Find the normal depth of flow \(y\) in meters.

Core Concepts:

Geometry: For the standard lined triangular section, the radius of the circular bottom equals \(y\) and the center of the arc lies at the free water surface. This gives a hydraulic radius that simplifies elegantly to \(R = y/2\).

Chezy's Equation: \(Q = C \cdot A \cdot \sqrt{R \cdot S}\)

Solution Method:

  1. Calculate angle \(\theta\): side slope has vertical = 1, horizontal = 1.5, so \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(1/1.5)\) (in radians).
  2. Determine area: \(A = y^2(\theta + \cot\theta)\).
  3. Determine hydraulic radius: \(R = y/2\).
  4. Substitute into Chezy's formula and solve for \(y\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Angle of normal:\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1.5}\right) = 0.588 \text{ rad}, \quad \cot\theta = 1.5\]

  2. Area calculation:\[A = y^2(0.588 + 1.5) = 2.088\, y^2\]

  3. Chezy's application:\[20 = 150 \cdot (2.088\,y^2) \cdot \sqrt{\dfrac{y}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{200}}\]\[20 = 313.2\,y^2 \cdot \dfrac{y^{0.5}}{20} = 15.66\, y^{2.5}\]\[y^{2.5} = \dfrac{20}{15.66} = 1.277\]\[y = (1.277)^{0.4} = 1.102 \text{ m}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.10 m | Accepted key range: 1.09 to 1.12

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A spillway has unit discharge of 7.5 m³/s/m. The flow depth at the downstream horizontal apron is 0.5 m. The tail water depth (in meters) required to form a hydraulic jump is ____________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Open Channel Flow | Hydraulic Jump

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Unit discharge \(q = 7.5\) m³/s/m
    • Initial flow depth \(y_1 = 0.5\) m
  • Aim: Calculate the tailwater depth (\(y_2\)) required for a hydraulic jump.

Core Concepts:

Froude Number (\(Fr\)): Ratio of inertial forces to gravity forces. \(Fr_1 = V_1 / \sqrt{g \cdot y_1}\)

Belanger Equation: Relates conjugate depths in a horizontal rectangular channel.\[y_2 = \dfrac{y_1}{2}\left(\sqrt{1 + 8Fr_1^2} - 1\right)\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial Velocity:\[V_1 = \dfrac{q}{y_1} = \dfrac{7.5}{0.5} = 15 \text{ m/s}\]

  2. Froude Number Squared:\[Fr_1^2 = \dfrac{V_1^2}{g \cdot y_1} = \dfrac{225}{9.81 \times 0.5} = \dfrac{225}{4.905} = 45.87\]

  3. Belanger Equation:\[y_2 = \dfrac{0.5}{2}\left(\sqrt{1 + 8(45.87)} - 1\right) = 0.25\left(\sqrt{367.96} - 1\right)\]\[y_2 = 0.25(19.182 - 1) = 0.25 \times 18.182 = 4.545 \text{ m}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.55 m | Accepted key range: 4.40 to 4.70

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A 5 m × 5 m closed tank of 10 m height contains water and oil, and is connected to an overhead water reservoir as shown in the figure. Use \( \gamma_w = 10 \text{ kN/m}^3 \) and Specific gravity of oil = 0.8.




The total force (in kN) due to pressure on the side PQR of the tank is ______________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Hydrostatic Forces

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Right tank: 5 m × 5 m base, closed top, 10 m height; connected to an overhead water reservoir
    • \(\gamma_w = 10\) kN/m³; Specific gravity of oil = 0.8, so \(\gamma_{oil} = 8\) kN/m³
  • Aim: Find the total hydrostatic pressure force on the face PQR.

Core Concepts:

  • Manometry & Pressure Transmission: Pressure from the left open tank transfers directly to the right closed tank via the connecting pipe.
  • Hydrostatic Pressure Distribution: Pressure increases linearly with depth (\(P = P_0 + \gamma \cdot h\)).
  • Force Calculation: Total force = area under the pressure diagram × width of the face.

Solution Method:

Pitfall Warning: Visual diagram interpretation is critical. Key geometry: the connecting pipe steps down 2m; the top pipe is 8m below the left free surface; oil layer thickness = 4m (R to Q); water layer thickness = 6m (Q to P); the pipe connects at interface Q.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Depth to Interface Q:\[\text{Depth to Q} = 8 + 2 = 10 \text{ m}\]

  2. Pressure at Q:\[P_Q = \gamma_w \cdot h = 10 \times 10 = 100 \text{ kPa}\]

  3. Pressure at Top (R) — moving up through oil:\[P_R = P_Q - \gamma_{oil} \cdot h_{oil} = 100 - (8 \times 4) = 68 \text{ kPa}\]

  4. Pressure at Bottom (P) — moving down through water:\[P_P = P_Q + \gamma_w \cdot h_{water} = 100 + (10 \times 6) = 160 \text{ kPa}\]

  5. Force on oil zone (R to Q), width = 5 m:\[F_{oil} = \dfrac{P_R + P_Q}{2} \cdot h_{oil} \cdot B = \dfrac{68 + 100}{2} \times 4 \times 5 = 84 \times 20 = 1680 \text{ kN}\]

  6. Force on water zone (Q to P), width = 5 m:\[F_{water} = \dfrac{P_Q + P_P}{2} \cdot h_{water} \cdot B = \dfrac{100 + 160}{2} \times 6 \times 5 = 130 \times 30 = 3900 \text{ kN}\]

  7. Total Force:\[F_{total} = 1680 + 3900 = 5580 \text{ kN}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 5580 kN | Accepted key range: 5575 to 5585

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q60
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
Activated carbon is used to remove a pollutant from wastewater in a mixed batch reactor, which follows first-order reaction kinetics.


At a reaction rate of 0.38 /day, the time (in days) required to remove the pollutant by 95% is _____________ (rounded off to 1 decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Kinetics

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Mixed batch reactor
    • First-order reaction kinetics
    • Reaction rate \(k = 0.38\) /day
    • Target removal = 95%
  • Aim: Calculate the time in days required to achieve 95% removal.

Core Concepts:

First-Order Kinetics: The concentration of pollutant over time follows the exponential decay model:\[C_t = C_0 \cdot e^{-kt}\]where \(C_t\) is final concentration, \(C_0\) is initial concentration, \(k\) is the rate constant, and \(t\) is time.

Solution Method:

A 95% removal means only 5% of the pollutant remains, so \(C_t / C_0 = 0.05\). Substitute into the rate equation and solve for \(t\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

\[0.05 = e^{-0.38\, t}\]

Taking the natural logarithm of both sides:

\[\ln(0.05) = -0.38\, t\]\[-2.9957 = -0.38\, t\]\[t = \dfrac{2.9957}{0.38} = 7.883 \text{ days} \approx 7.9 \text{ days}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 7.9 days | Accepted key range: 7.8 to 8.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q61
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
A water treatment plant treats 25 MLD water with a natural alkalinity of 4.0 mg/L (as CaCO₃). It is estimated that, during coagulation of this water, 450 kg/day of calcium bicarbonate (Ca(HCO₃)₂) is required based on the alum dosage.


Consider the atomic weights as: Ca-40, H-1, C-12, O-16.

The quantity of pure quick lime, CaO (in kg) required for this process per day is_____________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment (Coagulation)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Discharge, \(Q\) = 25 MLD
    • Natural alkalinity = 4.0 mg/L (as \(CaCO_3\))
    • \(Ca(HCO_3)_2\) required for alum dosage = 450 kg/day
    • Atomic weights: Ca-40, H-1, C-12, O-16
  • Aim: Find the quantity of pure quick lime (CaO) in kg required per day.

Core Concepts:

Equivalent Weights: In water chemistry, reacting masses are always proportional to their equivalent weights.\[\text{Equivalent Weight} = \dfrac{\text{Molecular Weight}}{\text{Valency}}\]

Alkalinity Supplementation: When natural alkalinity is insufficient to react with the added coagulant (alum), an external alkali — usually quick lime (CaO) — is added.\[\text{Deficit Alkalinity} = \text{Total Required Alkalinity} - \text{Natural Available Alkalinity}\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Equivalent Weights:

    • \(CaCO_3\): MW \(= 40 + 12 + 48 = 100\); valency = 2; EW = 50
    • \(Ca(HCO_3)_2\): MW \(= 40 + 2(1 + 12 + 48) = 162\); valency = 2; EW = 81
    • CaO: MW \(= 40 + 16 = 56\); valency = 2; EW = 28

  2. Calculate Natural Available Alkalinity:
    Total mass per day \(= 25 \times 10^6 \text{ L/day} \times 4.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ kg/L} = 100 \text{ kg/day as } CaCO_3\)
    In equivalents: \(\dfrac{100}{50} = 2.0 \text{ kEq/day}\)

  3. Calculate Total Required Alkalinity:
    Total required \(Ca(HCO_3)_2 = 450\) kg/day
    In equivalents: \(\dfrac{450}{81} = 5.555 \text{ kEq/day}\)

  4. Calculate Deficit to be supplied by CaO:\[\text{Deficit} = 5.555 - 2.0 = 3.555 \text{ kEq/day}\]\[\text{Mass of CaO} = 3.555 \times 28 = 99.55 \text{ kg/day}\]

Note: The GATE key also accepts 154–156 kg/day, which corresponds to ignoring natural alkalinity entirely and meeting the full 450 kg/day requirement with lime (\(5.555 \times 28 = 155.54\) kg/day). However, subtracting natural alkalinity is the physically accurate engineering approach.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 99.56 kg/day | Accepted key range: 99 to 100 OR 154 to 156

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q62
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
The number of trains and their corresponding speeds for a curved Broad Gauge section with 437 m radius, are

  • 20 trains travel at a speed of 40 km/hr
  • 15 trains travel at a speed of 50 km/hr
  • 12 trains travel at a speed of 60 km/hr
  • 8 trains travel at a speed of 70 km/hr
  • 3 trains travel at a speed of 80 km/hr

If the gauge (center-to-center distance between the rail heads) is taken as 1750 mm, the required equilibrium cant (in mm) will be _____________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Railway Engineering | Geometric Design

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Radius of curve, \(R\) = 437 m
    • Gauge distance, \(G\) = 1750 mm
    • Train distribution: 20 at 40 km/hr, 15 at 50 km/hr, 12 at 60 km/hr, 8 at 70 km/hr, 3 at 80 km/hr
  • Aim: Calculate the required equilibrium cant to the nearest integer.

Core Concepts:

Equilibrium Speed (\(V_{eq}\)): According to Indian Railways, the equilibrium speed is the weighted average of train speeds.\[V_{eq} = \dfrac{\sum (n_i \cdot V_i)}{\sum n_i}\]

Equilibrium Cant (\(e\)): Elevation of the outer rail over the inner rail to counteract centrifugal force.\[e = \dfrac{G \cdot V_{eq}^2}{127 \cdot R}\](\(G\) in mm, \(V\) in km/hr, \(R\) in m → \(e\) in mm)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total Number of Trains:\[N = 20 + 15 + 12 + 8 + 3 = 58 \text{ trains}\]

  2. Weighted Average Speed:\[\sum n_i V_i = (20 \times 40) + (15 \times 50) + (12 \times 60) + (8 \times 70) + (3 \times 80)\]\[= 800 + 750 + 720 + 560 + 240 = 3070\]\[V_{eq} = \dfrac{3070}{58} = 52.931 \text{ km/hr}\]

  3. Equilibrium Cant:\[e = \dfrac{1750 \times (52.931)^2}{127 \times 437} = \dfrac{1750 \times 2801.69}{55499} = \dfrac{4{,}902{,}957.5}{55499} = 88.34 \text{ mm}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 88 mm | Accepted key range: 86 to 90

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q63
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
The figure presents the trajectories of six vehicles within a time-space domain. The number in the parentheses represents unique identification of each vehicle.




The mean speed (in km/hr) of the vehicles in the entire time-space domain is ____________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Traffic Engineering | Traffic Flow Fundamentals

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: A time-space domain graphic showing trajectories of 6 distinct vehicles.
  • Aim: Determine the mean speed of all vehicles in the entire time-space domain in km/hr.

Core Concepts:

Space Mean Speed in a Domain (Edie's Definition): When calculating mean speed over a time-space area rather than at a single point:\[v_s = \dfrac{\sum d_i}{\sum t_i}\]where \(d_i\) is the distance covered by vehicle \(i\) inside the boundary, and \(t_i\) is the time spent by vehicle \(i\) inside the boundary.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Extract Data from Trajectories:

    VehicleStart (t, d)End (t, d)\(d_i\) (m)\(t_i\) (s)
    1(0s, 400m)(10s, 500m)10010
    2(0s, 250m)(15s, 500m)25015
    3(0s, 100m)(30s, 500m)40030
    4(5s, 0m)(30s, 400m)40025
    5(15s, 0m)(30s, 350m)35015
    6(20s, 0m)(30s, 150m)15010

  2. Sum Distances and Times:\[\sum d_i = 100 + 250 + 400 + 400 + 350 + 150 = 1650 \text{ m}\]\[\sum t_i = 10 + 15 + 30 + 25 + 15 + 10 = 105 \text{ s}\]

  3. Calculate Mean Speed:\[v_s = \dfrac{1650}{105} = 15.714 \text{ m/s}\]\[v_s = 15.714 \times 3.6 = 56.57 \text{ km/hr} \approx 57 \text{ km/hr}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 57 km/hr | Accepted key range: 52 to 58

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q64
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
The following data is obtained from an axle load survey at a site:

Average rear axle load = 12000 kg
Number of commercial vehicles = 800 per day

The pavement at this site would be reconstructed over a period of 5 years from the date of survey. The design life of the reconstructed pavement is 15 years. Use the standard axle load as 8160 kg and the annual average vehicle growth rate as 4.0%. Assume that Equivalent Wheel Load Factor (EWLF) and Vehicle Damage Factor (VDF) are equal.


The cumulative standard axle (in msa) for the pavement design is ______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Pavement Design

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Average rear axle load = 12000 kg
    • Commercial vehicles = 800 per day
    • Construction period, \(x\) = 5 years
    • Design life, \(n\) = 15 years
    • Standard axle load = 8160 kg
    • Traffic growth rate, \(r\) = 4% = 0.04
    • VDF = EWLF (Vehicle Damage Factor = Equivalent Wheel Load Factor)
  • Aim: Calculate the Cumulative Standard Axle (CSA) in msa.

Core Concepts:

Initial Traffic (\(A\)): \(A = P(1+r)^x\) where \(P\) is present traffic.

Vehicle Damage Factor (VDF) — 4th Power Rule:\[VDF = \left(\dfrac{\text{Axle Load}}{\text{Standard Axle Load}}\right)^4\]

Cumulative Standard Axles (CSA) — IRC 37 Formula:\[N = \dfrac{365 \cdot A \cdot [(1+r)^n - 1]}{r} \cdot VDF \cdot LDF \cdot LSF\]

Solution Method:

No Lane Distribution Factor (LDF) is provided, so LDF = 1.0 is assumed. Note: Due to a typographical error in the source paper and missing LDF data, GATE authorities declared this question MTA (Marks to All).

Step-by-Step Execution:

questions.question: A bird is resting on a point P at a height of 8 m above the Mean Sea Level (MSL). Upon hearing a loud noise, the bird flies parallel to the ground surface and reaches a point Q which is located at a height of 3 m above MSL. The ground surface has a falling gradient of 1 in 2. Ignoring the effects of curvature and refraction, the horizontal distance (in meters) between points P and Q is ___________ (in integer).
questions.explanation:
Surveying | Leveling & Gradients

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Bird's start elevation at P = 8 m above MSL
    • Bird's end elevation at Q = 3 m above MSL
    • Ground has a falling gradient of 1 in 2
    • Bird flies parallel to the ground surface
  • Aim: Horizontal distance between P and Q in integer meters.

Core Concepts:

Gradient Definition: A gradient of "1 in \(n\)" means a vertical drop of 1 unit for every \(n\) horizontal units.\[\text{Gradient} = \dfrac{\Delta V}{\Delta H}\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Vertical Drop (\(\Delta V\)):\[\Delta V = 8 \text{ m} - 3 \text{ m} = 5 \text{ m}\]

  2. Apply Gradient to find Horizontal Distance (\(\Delta H\)):
    Since the bird flies parallel to the ground with a gradient of 1 in 2:\[\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\Delta V}{\Delta H} \implies \Delta H = 2 \times \Delta V = 2 \times 5 = 10 \text{ m}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 10 m | Accepted key range: 10 to 10
